text: I'll start with the paged deployment and its pod.

remediation.name: recommendations
remediation.required_value: 256Mi (at least above the ~200Mi the warmup allocates; raise requests to match, e.g. 256Mi)

arguments.root_cause_statement: Deployment recs/recommendations runs a startup command that builds a 200 MiB in-memory catalog cache (`dd if=/dev/zero bs=1M count=200 | tr '\0' x`) while its container memory limit is set to 64Mi. The cgroup limit is exceeded during warmup, so the kernel OOM-kills the container before it prints "catalog cache ready" and reaches its serving loop. The pod recs/recommendations-85fd7764f4-p9rw8 therefore reports State Terminated / Reason OOMKilled / Exit Code 137 and Ready: False, kubelet CrashLoopBackOffs it ("Back-off restarting failed container server"), and the Deployment stays at 0/1 available with condition Available=False MinimumReplicasUnavailable — which is what the workload health monitor paged on and why the "You may also like" panel has no backend serving it.
arguments.mechanism: Deployment recs/recommendations sets .spec.template.spec.containers[server].resources.limits.memory to 64Mi while the same template's command allocates a ~200Mi cache (`dd if=/dev/zero bs=1M count=200 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' x`), so the container exceeds its cgroup limit during warmup and is killed with Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137 after logging only "warming catalog cache". Kubelet restarts it into "Back-off restarting failed container server", so the replica never passes Ready and the Deployment holds at "0 available | 1 unavailable".

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment has no available replica.
evidence.quote: Replicas:               1 desired | 1 updated | 1 total | 0 available | 1 unavailable

evidence.claim: The single pod's container is not ready and was OOM-killed twice.
The pod template asks for a 200 MiB allocation but caps memory at 64Mi.
evidence.quote: CACHE="$(dd if=/dev/zero bs=1M count=200 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' x)"

evidence.claim: The container memory limit in the Deployment template is 64Mi.
The container dies during cache warmup, before reaching the serving loop.
Kubelet keeps restarting the OOM-killed container, so the replica never becomes ready.
evidence.quote: Back-off restarting failed container server in pod recommendations-85fd7764f4-p9rw8_recs

ruled_out.alternative: Node memory exhaustion / node pressure evicting the pod
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The node has ~12 GiB allocatable memory and is Ready, so the kill came from the container's own cgroup limit, not node pressure.

ruled_out.alternative: A namespace LimitRange injecting or capping the memory limit
ruled_out.ruling_claim: No LimitRange exists in namespace recs, so the 64Mi limit comes from the Deployment's own template.
ruled_out.quote: 0 objects of kind limitranges in namespace recs

ruled_out.alternative: A ResourceQuota blocking or constraining the workload
ruled_out.ruling_claim: No ResourceQuota exists in namespace recs.
ruled_out.quote: 0 objects of kind resourcequotas in namespace recs

ruled_out.alternative: A missing ConfigMap/Secret/volume reference preventing startup
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The container declares no env, no mounts and no volumes beyond the default service account token, so no external reference can be failing to resolve.

verification.command: kubectl -n recs describe pod recommendations-85fd7764f4-p9rw8 | grep -A3 'Last State'
